predictions.text: Take Milwaukee on the money line, with Tampa Bay’s pitching a reason to keep expectations measured. Nick Martinez has conceded only three runs over nine road innings this postseason, and the Rays have won 24 of his 33 starts including the playoffs. The Brewers answer with Jacob Misiorowski, the regular-season ERA leader at 1.80, returning after eleven full days off. His most recent outing lasted only 4⅓ innings, so Milwaukee’s relief depth could matter: its bullpen has allowed six earned runs in 40⅔ postseason innings. The hosts arrive off a four-game NLCS sweep, with William Contreras batting .367 through eight playoff games. Tampa Bay are without Shane McClanahan for the postseason. Brandon Woodruff has made Milwaukee’s roster, but MLB describes continuing shoulder-related risk; his inclusion should not be treated as proof of full fitness. Milwaukee to win remains the selection, without a separate totals recommendation.
